contrary_evidence: October US ISM PMI 55.5 and production 59.0 signify stronger surveyed industry even as AI stocks and Nasdaq declined on Nov2; equity performance is not a real manufacturing output series.
Oil Brent -7.63% and WTI -7.36% reflect market expectations around Iran talks; no signed comprehensive peace accord or verified full transit restoration was established.
ISM input price index 75.2 fell from 77.9 yet remains an elevated diffusion index; not a 2.7% drop in prices or immediate disinflation.
Euro-area October PMI 52.7 and US55.5 remain expansionary, while French49.5 contracted; cannot claim a synchronized manufacturing recession.
Nasdaq -1.07 and S&P500 -0.51 but Dow +0.41 show cross-sector differences; no across-the-board US equity collapse on Nov2.
Brazil B3 was closed Nov2; domestic equity and dollar last verified session October30, not Monday.
US midterm results, Brazil Copom decision and Eurostat October flash estimate not yet published at 01:45 BRT cutoff.
Price futures, cargo volumes, physical oil stocks, official OPEC+ production requirements and actual production are distinct economic measures.
limitations: Information cutoff 3 November 2026 01:45 BRT; do not treat later US election returns, Asian opening, B3 trading or Central Bank/Eurostat releases as known at this timestamp.
S&P PMI euro-area and France details reported from Reuters where underlying subscription survey material is not fully open; ISM original directly checked.
Oil prices are November2 futures settlements and cannot establish current physical delivery, stored inventory totals or a concluded peace agreement.
Focus November3 release scheduled after cutoff; no new Focus median numbers claimed.
Brazil October30 closing levels and decline are dated and cannot stand for November3 live opening prices.
US manufacturing PMI, European factory diffusion and real GDP annualisation are methodologically different measures and cannot be converted into common output growth.
Foreign currency and corporate debt reactions are scenarios with contingencies, not point estimates or personal investment recommendations.

External verification sampled critical primary and dated Reuters sources; all 20 links checked for identity but some were not independently crawled for the complete article body. Deterministic GitHub Actions build still required before public deployment.

en.title: Global Macro — Oil's 7.6% decline exposes a split between industrial resilience and financing risk
en.deck: Brent's 7.63% fall, October US ISM 55.5 with prices 75.2, weaker Nasdaq, divergent European industry and pending US midterms and Brazil Copom reveal a global battle between energy relief and the cost of finance.
en.regime: Strong industrial US activity and uneven euro-area growth coexist with elevated input costs, a sharp geopolitical oil-price fall and renewed concern about debt-funded AI investment.
